## Summary
Document the ownership model and the expected show/hide behavior for the Gym SLL demo.

Contributors can follow the documented pattern instead of adding more ad hoc chrome visibility logic.

- **Tests**: Ensure any referenced commands or snippets match the real test targets.
- **Docs**: Update `example-games/gym/README.md` and `docs/DEVELOPER.md` with ownership/visibility guidance.
- **Infra**: Reuse the existing docs structure.

- SLL guidance in `docs/DEVELOPER.md`
- browser tests for the Gym demo

Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.
data.title: Gym Hand & Pile: selection highlight raises with the card; raise slider max 180 / default 60

# Scaffold write classification, `--dry-run` and a machine-readable report

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — engine slice covering AC1 (`--dry-run`), AC2 and the dry-run half of AC4.

## Target outcome

A scaffold run classifies every file it generates **before** touching the disk, returns that classification in its typed result and prints it for every run; `--dry-run` performs the identical classification and writes nothing.

## Behaviour contract

- Generated-file set unchanged: `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `env.d.ts`, `main.ts`, `index.html` (still copied from `core/index.html`) and `configs/game.json`.
- Classification vocabulary is fixed by the parent AC and must keep this shape in later slices: `create` (target absent), `update` (exists and differs from the template → written), `unchanged` (exists, byte-identical), `skip-local` (exists and differs, not written). This slice produces only `create` / `update` / `unchanged`; the `skip-local` discriminator and the `--force` gate that produces it are the next slice.
- `ScaffoldResult` gains `files: ScaffoldFileReport[]` (`{ path, action }`, repo-relative, stable order). The existing `written` array remains as a compatibility projection of the `create` + `update` entries.
- `--dry-run` performs no `mkdirSync`, no `fs.writeFileSync`, no symlink creation, no asset/public link and no path rewrite; `written` / `symlinks` / `assetLinks` / `publicLinks` / `rewritten` come back empty while `files` carries what a real run would do.
- `--json` prints one JSON document for the run (object for a single `--game`, array for `--all`) carrying the same `files` report; human output keeps one line per file (`  create  main.ts`).
- Inline rationale comment in the generator explains **why** writes are classified and gated (a live consumer checkout owns its wiring, so only opted-in files may change) rather than overwritten blindly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC2 carried over verbatim — **Write reporting.** Every run (dry or real) prints a machine-readable summary of the classification per file, so a consumer can see what a run would touch before trusting it. _(covered by this slice (machine-readable per-file report for dry and real runs).)_
- Parent AC4 carried over verbatim — **Engine tests (test-first).** `core/tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` gains tests written **before** the implementation for: `--only` restricting writes, `--dry-run` writing nothing while classifying correct, `--force` required to replace a diverged file, default-on-path-rewrite removed (no-op without the flag) and preserved with the flag. The full engine suite passes. _(this child writes the classification, `--dry-run` and report tests; the sibling children write the `--only`/`--force` and rewrite-opt-in tests, so AC4 closes only when all three engine children are green.)_
- Tests are authored **before** the implementation in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (RED first, then GREEN) covering: an absent file classifies `create` and is created; a byte-identical file classifies `unchanged` and is not rewritten; a diverged file classifies `update` and is overwritten; the `files` report covers every generated file.
- `scaffoldGameRepo({ dryRun: true })` on a temp repo leaves every protected file byte-identical (checksum comparison), creates no `core` symlink, no asset links and performs no path rewrite, while `files` reports the classification the following real run applies.
- A real run's `files` report equals the preceding `--dry-run` report for the same tree (no classification drift between dry and real runs).
- CLI: `--dry-run --json` against a temp repo writes nothing and emits a single parseable JSON document containing a `files` array; `--help` documents `--dry-run` and `--json`.
- The targeted unit run (`/skill:test --type unit` scoped to `tests/scripts/`) and `npm run build` pass; the full engine suite passes at the `dev` push gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Replace the `writeFile(path, contents, written)` helper with a `classifyAndApply(path, contents, opts)` step returning a `ScaffoldFileReport`, and keep `writeFile` as a thin wrapper so existing call sites stay readable.
- Add `dryRun?: boolean` to `ScaffoldOptions`; thread it through the whole `scaffoldGameRepo` body (file writes, `core` symlink, asset links, public links, path rewrite).
- Export `ScaffoldFileReport` / `ScaffoldFileAction` types; add `files` to `ScaffoldResult`.
- `parseArgs`: `--dry-run`, `--json`; `usage()` entries; `main()` prints the per-file report and the JSON document.
- Tests: extend the existing `scaffoldGameRepo` / `linkShared*` fixtures in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` with a temp-repo harness that pre-seeds generated files, then assert classification, no-write behaviour and dry-vs-real equality.

## Prototype/Experiment

None required — the classification is a byte comparison over a fixed, small file set.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — classification pipeline, `dryRun` option, `files` report, CLI flags, rationale comment.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — new classification/dry-run/report tests (authored first).

## Dependencies

None — this is the first engine slice.

## Deliverables

Typed per-file classification in `ScaffoldResult`, a `--dry-run` mode that writes nothing, a `--json` machine-readable report for both dry and real runs, and green targeted unit + build gates.
data.title: Scaffold write classification, dry-run and report

# `--only` allow-list, `--force` and `skip-local` write gating

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — engine slice covering the `--only` / `--force` / `skip-local` half of AC1 (and AC4).

## Target outcome

A consumer checkout can opt in to exactly the generated files it wants regenerated. Selecting a subset never touches anything else — no other file, no symlink, no asset link and no path rewrite — and a selected file whose local content differs from the template is only overwritten when the caller explicitly asks for it.

## Behaviour contract

- `ScaffoldOptions.only?: string[]` / CLI `--only <file,...>`. Names are repo-relative generated paths (`main.ts`, `configs/game.json`, `index.html`, …). Selecting a file is the **only** way a run may modify a consumer-owned file.
- Unselected generated files classify `skip-local` and are not written.
- `ScaffoldOptions.force?: boolean` / CLI `--force`. A **selected** file that exists and differs from the template is `skip-local` (not written) unless `--force` is passed, in which case it is `update` (written). Without `--force` the run cannot silently clobber a hand-edited generated file.
- Back-compatibility is preserved exactly: with **no** `--only`, a run behaves as today — every diverged generated file is rewritten — because the eight sibling `tce-<game>` repos rely on a plain full run to receive template updates. Implement this as `effectiveForce = force || only === undefined` and document it in the help text and inline comments (a full run is inherently the "regenerate everything" mode).
- `--only` suppresses all non-file side effects: no `core` symlink creation, no shared-asset links, no root app-icon links, no game-tree path rewrite. The run reports that it skipped them (a one-line note; `symlinks` / `assetLinks` / `publicLinks` / `rewritten` come back empty).
- An unknown name in `--only` fails fast (exit code 1) with a message listing the valid generated paths, and nothing is written — a typo must not produce a silent no-op scaffold.
- Classification reporting from the previous slice is unchanged; `--only` + `--dry-run` reports the same classification the real `--only` run would apply.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC1 carried over verbatim — **Generator write gating.** `scaffoldGameRepo`/the CLI accept `--only <file,...>` (restrict the run to the named generated files; no other file, symlink or rewrite is performed), `--force` (allow overwriting a file whose content differs from the template) and `--dry-run` (report every file as `create | update | unchanged | skip-local`, writing nothing). Default behaviour for extracted repos is unchanged: a full scaffold still writes all generated files. _(this slice delivers the `--only`, `--force` and `skip-local` clauses plus the unchanged full-run default.)_
- Tests are authored **before** the implementation in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (RED first, then GREEN) for: `--only main.ts` writing only `main.ts` while every other generated file stays byte-identical and classifies `skip-local`; no `core` symlink / asset link / path rewrite being created in selection mode.
- A diverged selected file stays untouched (`skip-local`) without `--force` and is regenerated (`update`) with `--force`.
- An unknown `--only` name throws / exits 1 with the valid-name list and leaves the temp repo byte-identical.
- A full run (no `--only`) still rewrites a diverged generated file (explicit regression guard for the eight sibling repos), and a full run on an unchanged tree classifies every file `unchanged` and writes nothing.
- `--only main.ts --dry-run` writes nothing and its report matches the following real run's report.
- The targeted unit run (`/skill:test --type unit` scoped to `tests/scripts/`) and `npm run build` pass; the full engine suite passes at the `dev` push gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `only?: string[]` and `force?: boolean` to `ScaffoldOptions`; derive `effectiveForce` and an `isSelected(relPath)` predicate in `scaffoldGameRepo`.
- Route every generated write through the selection predicate; skip the `core` symlink, `linkSharedAssets`, `linkSharedPublicAssets` and `rewriteGameTreePaths` calls when `only` is set, and print the "selection mode" note.
- Validate `--only` names against the generated set up front (before any write) and throw with the sorted valid list; `parseArgs` also enforces that `--only` implies literal names (no globs).
- `parseArgs` / `usage()`: `--only <file,...>` and `--force`, including the note that a full run implies force.
- Tests: extend the classification harness with mismatched-content fixtures and CLI-level assertions (spawn or `parseArgs` + `scaffoldGameRepo` on a temp repo).

## Prototype/Experiment

None required.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `only` / `force` options, selection predicate, side-effect suppression, `skip-local` classification, validation and rationale comments.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — selection/force/`skip-local` tests (authored first).

## Dependencies

- `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` child: _Scaffold write classification, --dry-run and machine-readable report_ — supplies the classification pipeline this slice extends.

## Deliverables

`--only` / `--force` gating with `skip-local` classification, fail-fast validation of selected names, unchanged full-run behaviour for extracted repos, and green targeted unit + build gates.
data.title: Only allow-list, force and skip-local gating

# Gate the game-tree path rewrite behind `--migrate-game-paths`

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — engine slice covering AC3 (and the opt-in half of AC4).

## Target outcome

`scaffoldGameRepo` no longer rewrites `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` (or the accompanying quoted-path, alias and `scripts/` rewrites) unless the caller explicitly asks for a migration, so a routine re-scaffold can never edit a consumer's tests or source.

## Behaviour contract

- `ScaffoldOptions.migrateGamePaths?: boolean` / CLI `--migrate-game-paths`; **default off**.
- Without the flag `rewriteGameTreePaths()` is not invoked at all: no file under `tests/` or `src/` is modified and `rewritten` is empty. Fresh repos do not need it — `scripts/extract-repos.sh --path-rename` already produced the `src/` layout.
- With the flag the current rewrite behaviour is preserved verbatim (all four textual rewrites) and the affected files are reported both in `ScaffoldResult.rewritten` and as report entries.
- `--migrate-game-paths --dry-run` writes nothing but reports the files a real migration would rewrite (and which rewrite would apply), so a maintainer can preview a migration.
- `--only` and `--migrate-game-paths` are mutually exclusive: `--only` promises "no rewrite", so a run passing both fails fast (exit 1) with an explanatory message rather than half-migrating a repo.
- The exported `rewriteGameTreePaths()` signature is unchanged (other tooling and tests import it directly); only the unconditional call inside `scaffoldGameRepo` is gated.
- Rationale comment in the generator explains why the rewrite became opt-in (the blanket rewrite touched files with no genuine game-tree reference — a drift guard's own `STALE_PREFIX`, run-tests imports, documented local edits).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Parent AC3 carried over verbatim — **Path rewrite is opt-in.** `example-games/<game>/` → `src/` and the accompanying quoted-path/alias rewrites run only with `--migrate-game-paths`; without it, no file under `tests/` or `src/` is modified. `--migrate-game-paths` also reports the files it rewrites. _(this slice delivers the opt-in flag and its reporting.)_
- Tests are authored **before** the implementation in `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` (RED first, then GREEN) for: a default scaffold leaving a temp repo's `tests/**` and `src/**` files byte-identical while `rewritten` is empty; the same tree rewritten with `--migrate-game-paths` and the changed files reported; and a no-genuine-reference file (e.g. a fixture containing the literal `STALE_PREFIX`) staying byte-identical in both modes unless it genuinely contains `example-games/<game>/`.
- `--migrate-game-paths --dry-run` writes nothing and reports the files a real migration would rewrite.
- `--only main.ts --migrate-game-paths` fails fast with a non-zero exit and writes nothing.
- `--help` documents `--migrate-game-paths`, its default-off status and the mutual exclusion with `--only`.
- The targeted unit run (`/skill:test --type unit` scoped to `tests/scripts/`) and `npm run build` pass; the full engine suite passes at the `dev` push gate.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `migrateGamePaths?: boolean` to `ScaffoldOptions`; replace the unconditional `rewriteGameTreePaths(gameRepoRoot, options.game)` call with `options.migrateGamePaths ? … : []` and a documented rationale comment.
- Extend the classification/report pipeline so a migration run lists the rewritten files (dry-run listed, not written).
- `parseArgs`: `--migrate-game-paths`; reject it together with `--only`; extend `usage()`.
- Tests: extend the temp-repo harness with a `tests/` + `src/` fixture that carries genuine `example-games/<game>/` references and one that carries a decoy (`STALE_PREFIX`, `scripts/run-tests`).

## Prototype/Experiment

None required — the rewrite itself already exists; this slice only changes when it runs.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — `migrateGamePaths` option, gated call, dry-run reporting, mutual exclusion, rationale comment.
- `tests/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.test.ts` — rewrite opt-in/no-op/preview tests (authored first).

## Dependencies

- `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` child: _--only allow-list, --force and skip-local write gating_ — selection mode already suppresses rewrites; this slice adds the explicit migration flag and the mutual-exclusion guard.

## Deliverables

An opt-in `--migrate-game-paths` migration with a default-off, no-op-when-absent contract, dry-run preview, mutual exclusion with `--only`, and green targeted unit + build gates.
data.title: Gate path rewrite behind migrate-game-paths

# Document scaffold write gating in the engine docs

**Parent:** `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` — the documentation clause of AC5, applied to the engine repository (the consumer-side docs live in the `tce-main-street` follow-up `MS-0MVWGI4CB0055IT0`).

## Target outcome

Every engine-repo document that describes the scaffold command documents the new contract: default behaviour for extracted repos is unchanged, `--only` / `--force` gate consumer-owned files, `--dry-run` + `--json` report before writing, and `--migrate-game-paths` is the explicit, opt-in migration.

## Behaviour contract (what the docs must state)

- A **full run** (no `--only`) keeps today's behaviour and is the supported upgrade path for the eight sibling `tce-<game>` repos.
- A **selected run** (`--only <file,...>`) writes only the named generated files; every other file is `skip-local`, and no symlink, asset link or path rewrite is performed.
- `--force` is required to overwrite a selected file whose content differs from the template.
- `--dry-run` writes nothing; `--json` emits the machine-readable per-file classification (`create | update | unchanged | skip-local`) for both dry and real runs.
- `--migrate-game-paths` is opt-in and mutually exclusive with `--only`; fresh repos are already renamed by `extract-repos.sh --path-rename`.
- A worked example of the consumer pattern:
  `tsx core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts --game main-street --game-repo-root . --core-root ./core --only main.ts --force`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` §5 (per-game repo scaffold) documents the four flags, the unchanged default and the opt-in migration, and its existing example block stays accurate.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (per-game repo scaffold block) and the `README.md` scaffold example document the flags and the consumer pattern; neither still implies that a plain run is always safe in a live checkout.
- Each of `--only`, `--force`, `--dry-run`, `--json` and `--migrate-game-paths` appears at least once in both `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`.
- No document still claims the scaffold rewrites `tests/` or `src/` unconditionally.
- The generator's header comment links the flag contract to the docs section (a reader of the code finds the prose, and vice versa).
- `npm run build` passes and no documentation-only change breaks the docs/assets checks.

## Minimal Implementation

- Update the §5 scaffold section in `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`: a short "write gating" subsection plus the worked consumer example.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md`'s per-game scaffold block and the `README.md` scaffold example with the flags and the default/opt-in distinction.
- Add the cross-reference comment in the `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` header (the CLI block gains the new flags).

**Key Files:**

- `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md` — §5 scaffold contract.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — per-game repo scaffold block.
- `README.md` — scaffold quick-start example.
- `scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts` — header comment cross-reference.

## Dependencies

- `CG-0MVWFN1HX004B5PN` child: _Gate the game-tree path rewrite behind --migrate-game-paths_ — documents the final flag set.

## Deliverables

Engine documentation that accurately describes default vs. opted-in scaffold behaviour, with a copy-pasteable consumer example and a code↔docs cross-reference.
data.title: Document scaffold write gating in engine docs

# Register 1916: The Rising in the game-collection contract

## Problem statement

`../tce-the-rising` is a complete, playable example game and is already listed in
`configs/full.json` and its own per-game preset, yet it is **absent from
`scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`** — the single source of truth for the game
*collection* used by extraction, publication, distribution bootstrap and launcher
asset composition. As a result the distribution never clones it, never publishes it,
and never composes its game-owned assets, so under `GAMES_CONFIG=full` the Game
Selector card for 1916: The Rising has a 404 thumbnail and the game's SFX silently
fall back to `audio/default/`.

## Users

- **Producer / developer bootstrapping a distribution** — expects
  `npm run setup:distribution -- --dir ..` to restore *every* game in the collection.
- **Player of the `full` distribution** — expects The Rising's selector art and its
  own audio profile to load like every other game.
- **Release / publication maintainer** — expects the published repo set and docs to
  match the collection contract.

User stories:

- As a developer setting up a fresh multi-game distribution, I want the bootstrap to
  clone `tce-the-rising` so a "full" checkout is genuinely complete.
- As a player, I want The Rising's thumbnail, card backs and SFX to load in the merged
  launcher instead of falling back to shared defaults.
- As a maintainer, I want a guard test so a game added to `configs/full.json` can never
  again be forgotten in the collection contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Collection contract.** `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` carries a `games`
  entry for `the-rising` (`slug: tce-the-rising`, remote
  `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-the-rising.git`, `paths` for the delivered tree,
  `assets: ["audio/the-rising/", "games/the-rising/"]`) plus a matching `gameAssets`
  entry, so `loadDistributionTargets()`, `publish:repos`, `extract-repos.sh` and
  `planGameAssetLinks()` all resolve **nine** games.
- **AC2 — Asset composition.** With `GAMES_CONFIG=full`, `composeGameAssets` links
  `public/assets/audio/the-rising/` and `public/assets/games/the-rising/` (thumbnail,
  card backs, portraits) from the sibling checkout; a unit test proves the plan
  contains both roots and that the declared `GAME_INFO.thumbnail` key
  (`games/the-rising/thumbnail`) resolves to the composed
  `public/assets/games/the-rising/thumbnail.png` — the selector appends the `.png`
  (`assets/<thumbnail>.png` in `GameSelectorScene`), so the key itself carries no
  extension. Read the key through the discovery layer (`discoverGames`) rather than
  grepping the sibling's source, so the test is not a source-text assertion.
- **AC3 — Drift guard.** A new guard test asserts (a) every game id in
  `configs/full.json` has a `repo-layout.json` entry, (b) every `repo-layout.json`
  game has a per-game preset `configs/<id>.json`, and (c) every preset game is
  reachable at `../tce-<id>` — so contract, presets and presets' game lists cannot
  drift silently.
- **AC4 — Collection fixtures.** Hard-coded eight-game lists in the collection's own
  tests are updated to include `tce-the-rising`: `setup-distribution` (`GAME_SLUGS`),
  `repo-publication` (the "exactly the eight tce-<game> repos" list **and** the
  `toHaveLength(9)` target count, which becomes **10** = core + nine games),
  `link-game-assets` (ownership key set), `extract-repos` (`GAME_NAMES`), and the
  `distribution-presets` "all 8 games" wording/boundary count (one game and **nine**
  games) are corrected.
- **AC5 — Docs.** The ninth game is recorded in `docs/dev/multi-repo-architecture.md`
  (target-layout tree, game count, published-remotes table),
  `docs/dev/repo-publication-decision.md` (the fresh-sibling-clone `for g in …` loop
  in §5) and `docs/dev/per-game-src-layout-decision.md` (count wording — only the
  current-state "the full preset spans all eight games" sentence; the Option-C
  migration paragraph below it is a historical record of that migration and stays
  at eight, likewise the superseded "nine-repository publication" wording in
  `repo-publication-decision.md`).
- **AC6 — Validation.** New/updated tests pass through the test skill
  (`/skill:test --type unit`) and `npm run build` succeeds (including the
  `check:ui-node-surface` prebuild gate).
- **AC7 — Documentation policy.** All documentation affected by the change is updated in
  the same commit: the three distribution docs named in AC5, plus any comment or doc
  comment that enumerates the collection (e.g. the `distribution-presets.test.ts`
  header "all 8 games" wording and the `extract-repos.test.ts` "exactly the eight
  example games" test title). `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`,
  `public/assets/CREDITS.md` and `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` already document the game and
  already say "all nine games" — verify, do not rewrite.
- **AC8 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Core-repo change only; the sibling game already exists, is pushed, and needs no source
  changes (only its checkout must be present to run the asset tests).
- `repo-layout.json` stays the single source of truth — no new hard-coded game lists;
  derive from the contract wherever practical.
- `GAMES_CONFIG=core-only` must remain clean (no leftover `the-rising` asset symlinks
  after switching presets back).
- Push to `dev` only; do not edit `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/`, or agent infrastructure.
- `scripts/codemod-src-imports.ts`'s `GAME_NAMES` stays at eight deliberately: it is the
  historical monorepo→`src/` codemod, and The Rising never had a monorepo tree.

## Existing state

- `configs/the-rising.json` and the `full.json` entry exist (F8, CG-0MV0EKC08004A0BD).
- `README.md`, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `docs/dev/game-configuration.md`,
  `public/assets/CREDITS.md` and `docs/SFX_CONVENTION.md` already document the game and
  already say "all nine games"; the collection contract and its docs are the outliers.
- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` lists only the original eight games; `gameAssets`
  lists eight asset sets (no `the-rising`).
- `public/assets/games/` is empty and `public/assets/audio/` has no `the-rising/` —
  game assets are composed from sibling checkouts at build time, so the missing
  `gameAssets` entry is exactly why nothing is composed.
- The sibling ships `public/assets/audio/the-rising/` (13 WAVs) and
  `public/assets/games/the-rising/` (`thumbnail.png`, two card backs, `portraits/`),
  and `GAME_INFO.thumbnail = 'games/the-rising/thumbnail'`.
- Hard-coded eight-game lists: `tests/scripts/setup-distribution.test.ts` (`GAME_SLUGS`),
  `tests/scripts/repo-publication.test.ts` (two lists),
  `tests/scripts/link-game-assets.test.ts`, `tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts`.
- `scripts/link-game-assets.ts → planGameAssetLinks` **silently skips** a selected game
  with no ownership entry (`continue`), which is why the gap is invisible today.

## Desired change

One implementation change set that registers The Rising in the collection contract,
propagates it through the collection's fixtures, adds the drift guard, and updates the
three distribution docs.

**Implementation order (test-first — write the failing assertion before the change it
drives):**

1. Drift guard first (AC3): add the guard test; it fails on the current tree because
   `full.json` has nine games and `repo-layout.json` has eight — this is the
   reproduction of the bug.
2. Contract change (AC1): add the `games` + `gameAssets` entries; the guard and the
   `link-game-assets` ownership fixture (AC4) now turn green.
3. Fixture/count corrections (AC4) for the remaining eight-game lists.
4. Asset-composition proof (AC2) against the sibling checkout.
5. Docs (AC5, AC7).
6. Validation (AC6) then the full suite (AC8).

**Optional, not required by any AC:** `assetDecisionTable` has no
`games/the-rising/` row, but it is already not exhaustive (several existing games have
no `games/<game>/` row either), so adding one is optional polish and must not gate
completion.

**Decision already made for the `paths` risk** — the guard is the constraint, not a
guess: `tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts` ("assigns each game its own
example-games subtree") requires every game's `paths` to contain
`example-games/<name>`. See the mitigation under *Risks & assumptions*.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — `paths` semantics.** `repo-layout.json → paths` drives the historical
  monorepo extraction (`git filter-repo`). The Rising never existed in the monorepo, so
  an empty or invented path list could mislead `extract-repos.sh`.
  *Mitigation:* `tests/scripts/extract-repos.test.ts` ("assigns each game its own
  example-games subtree") asserts every `games[].paths` contains
  `example-games/<name>`, and `extract-repos.sh` passes `paths` straight to
  `git filter-repo --path`, so extraction is a historical one-off (the eight games are
  already extracted). Declare `paths` as the delivered repo tree
  (`example-games/the-rising`, `tests/the-rising`, `docs/the-rising`) so the contract
  and its test agree, and record in the work item that extraction for this entry is a
  no-op because the game never lived in the monorepo. Do **not** declare `[]` — that
  would require weakening the existing test.
- **Risk — silent skip hides future gaps.** `planGameAssetLinks` reports nothing for a
  selected game with no ownership entry. *Mitigation:* AC3's guard covers the drift; a
  richer report is optional and out of scope unless it is a one-line change.
- **Risk — private sibling repo.** `gh repo view` reports `tce-the-rising` as **private**
  while the documented publication contract says the game repos are public, so
  `setup:distribution` for a third party would fail to clone. Out of scope for the code
  change (see Open questions); the guard skips unreachable siblings.
- **Assumption —** the game keeps shipping its assets from its own repo; no copies land
  in the core's `public/assets` (matches every other game and the composition plugin).
- **Assumption —** the sibling checkout `../tce-the-rising` exists in this environment, so
  the asset-composition test can run (guard it like the existing preset tests do via
  `HAS_ANY_GAME_CHECKOUT`).
- **Scope-creep risk —** private visibility, `electron/bonus-catalog.json` and
  `electron/achievement-manifest.json` entries, and the `codemod-src-imports` list are
  *not* part of this change; record them as linked follow-ups rather than widening scope.
